subject: Cognitive Science
title: Attachment Theory
description: A quick win: understand Attachment Theory.

hook.text: A baby cries when Mom leaves and calms when she returns. That bond is hardwired for survival.

buildup.text: John Bowlby proposed that infants form attachments to ensure protection from a caregiver.

discovery.text: Ainsworth's Strange Situation test revealed three styles: secure, anxious, and avoidant.

twist.text: Secure attachment predicts better friendships, grades, and mental health decades later.

climax.text: Early attachment creates a mental model of relationships the child carries into adulthood.

punchline.text: First bonds shape all bonds after.

quiz.question: Who created the Strange Situation test?

details.summary: Bowlby proposed that infants form emotional bonds with caregivers that serve as a secure base for exploration. Ainsworth identified secure, avoidant, and anxious attachment styles through the Strange Situation experiment.
details.whyItMatters: Early attachment shapes emotional and social development far beyond childhood. Secure attachment predicts better relationships, resilience, and mental health outcomes in adulthood.
takeaways: Infants form attachment bonds that serve as a secure base
The Strange Situation identified three main attachment styles

faq.question: What is the Strange Situation experiment?
faq.answer: Ainsworth observed infants in a room with their caregiver, a stranger, and brief separations. Securely attached babies explored confidently and sought comfort upon reunion. Avoidant babies showed little distress; anxious babies were inconsolable.

faq.question: Can attachment styles change over time?
faq.answer: Yes. While early attachment creates a working model for relationships, significant life experiences like therapy, new relationships, or trauma can shift attachment patterns.
